title: Geology
subtitle: Mysteries in the rocks
summary: How geologists learned to read rock, told through the arguments that settled each question. James Hutton stood at Siccar Point in 1788 and saw that the Earth was unimaginably old; Kelvin spent decades insisting it was young; Alfred Wegener said the continents moved, and was dismissed until stripes on the seafloor, thirty years after his death, showed that they do. The twenty trunk lessons run from mud turning into rock to the 1964 earthquake that lifted an Alaskan coast out of the sea. After them come branches on the Pacific Northwest (Whidbey Island's bluffs, Seattle's hills and faults, the ice age floods that cut the scablands, Cascadia's earthquake of 1700), on the Moon, and on how anyone found out what is inside the Earth.

release.note: First release: all 47 lessons written, read through and fact-checked.
